directions.title: A — Porcelain daylight
directions.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: faithful visual concept preview for an interactive Three.js portfolio website. Input image 1 is the exact composition and camera reference, not a moodboard. Make ONE complete landscape website scene, same framing and aspect ratio as reference. Preserve the continuous endless spiral ribbon's path, number of turns, portal locations, approximate relative scales, asymmetric arch/cloud/leaf/oval/hourglass silhouettes, and the small central tetrahedral audio sculpture. Retain the generous areas of empty sky. Remove the small black Next.js developer badge. No browser chrome, text, logos, labels, UI panels, people, railings, extra buildings, particles everywhere, or detached ornate props. This must look like a plausible high-end real-time WebGL scene for M4 computers and A18/A19 mobile: smooth finite geometry, baked material detail, environment reflections, subtle contact shading, layered image clouds. No extravagant ray-traced caustics, depth of field, lens flares, motion blur, volumetric god rays, or film grain. Clearly model each portal physically meeting the ribbon with a tiny smoothly integrated fitted foot, no hovering gaps, no pedestals. Refine bevels and material response. Atmosphere and object illumination must agree. The central tetrahedron should be small and materially integrated rather than a flat black dominant shape. Render an achievable art-directed design proposal, not an impossible cinematic fantasy.
Direction A: preserve the current bright blue/cream cloud-world identity while making the finish exceptional. A transparent pale aqua cast-glass ribbon with a softly beveled visible edge and enough underside shading to carry weight. Portal frames made of satin ivory glazed porcelain, subtly varying rounded cross-section and clean tactile finish; thin champagne metal recessed lining with a fine dark seam. Delicate lightly frosted amber, sage, lavender, blush and ice-blue panes, with clear polished thickness edges and subdued interior reflections. Each frame flows into its small porcelain contact foot. Daylight is luminous but has a motivated warm upper-left key and cool blue shadow sides. Clouds below are natural vapor with varied density, crisp near detail and soft distant edges, less foamy and yellow than the source. Keep the quiet blue open sky. Central tetrahedron is warm pewter with subtle blue and ivory reflections. This is a conservative, faithful premium refinement, not a redesign.

Direction B: a bold but restrained sculptural architecture direction. Keep the exact spiral composition, but transform the ribbon into an impossibly thin carved warm-ivory alabaster/limestone ramp, satin and mostly opaque, with a soft rounded luminous edge and clearly shaded underside. No busy marble veining. Portal surrounds are hand-shaped cream porcelain/alabaster with asymmetrically tapering profiles, seamlessly rooted into tiny organic junctions of the ribbon. Very thin muted bronze/champagne inset reveals. Panes resemble pale translucent honey, rose quartz, sage and milky lavender cast glass; the surface is quiet and tactile, never opaque paint. Lighting is late-afternoon editorial architecture photography: warm highlights, gently cool taupe/blue shade, clear form and soft contact occlusion. Background is a pale apricot-to-pearl sky over a restrained sea of thinner misty clouds, less dense and decorative than the original, still ample negative space. Central tetrahedron is lightly brushed bronze. The design should feel collectible, architectural, calm and materially believable. No monuments, columns, extra landings, or heavy ornament.

Direction C: a bold blue-hour nocturne preview of the same website, keeping the exact reference spiral and portal composition. The ribbon becomes translucent smoke-quartz glass, edges catch fine cool silver highlights, its gently shaded underside and tiny warm contact joints remain legible. Thin sculptural satin-platinum portal surrounds with softer changing profiles, a very subtle warm champagne inner seam, softly tinted translucent glass in muted amber, lavender and sea green. Cool deep indigo/steel-blue sky fading to a faint rose-pearl horizon; layered lower clouds are charcoal blue and lilac vapor with delicate silver rim light, not a black void. Sparse tiny stars only in the upper sky, at most one delicate distant meteor. Keep the whole architecture readable and enough open sky; no neon strips or bright halos. Porcelain-like interior bevel surfaces and warm subtle inset glows balance moonlit metal. Central tetrahedron is softly reflective smoky silver. This is a sophisticated calm twilight environment, never sci-fi game UI or cyberpunk. Maintain local material detail and realistic real-time rendering limits.

Direction D: the boldest material redesign, a surreal editorial sculpture garden in a bright pearl sky. Keep exactly the spiral path, camera and portal positions, but form the ribbon from flowing satin silver with softly convex sections and a delicate mirrored edge; the broad surfaces have large smooth environmental reflections rather than noisy perfect mirror reflections. Portal frames are slim liquid-polished silver, organically tapering, each visibly melting into a tiny integrated foot on the ribbon. Their inner glazing is extremely pale rose, warm honey, ice blue and opal lavender, with more transparency than the source and clear optical edge depth. No bulky ivory surrounds and no thick gold trim. Lighting comes from huge pearl-white and cool-blue sky fields with one restrained warm highlight, producing confident dark-to-light bands that describe the sculpted metal. Background is high-key pearl with a very subtle cool lavender upper sky and natural, airy clouds low below the ramp. Spacious, dreamlike, contemporary collectible design; no chrome spikes, no extra blobs, no liquid drips, no iridescent rainbow clutter. Central tetrahedron is the same satin silver, small and understated. Prioritize believable simple environment-map reflections rather than expensive reflected copies of every object.
